main_results.N1: ae_hausdorffMeasure_inter_levelSet_eq_zero_of_lipschitz_pieces: if S is measurable, mu_H[n] S is finite, dim W2 > 0, and at every scale epsilon the composite Q . u is epsilon-Lipschitz on the pieces of a countable measurable partition of S, then for almost every tau in W2 the slice S intersect {Q . u = tau} is mu_H[n - dim W2]-null. No regularity whatever is assumed of u.
main_results.one_scale: exists_measurable_majorant_of_lipschitz_pieces: at a single scale the slice function is dominated by a MEASURABLE majorant of integral at most C * epsilon^(dim W2) * mu_H[n] S, obtained by summing the repository's codimension-m Eilenberg majorants over the pieces. The slice function itself is not known to be measurable, which is why the bound is carried by a majorant. Measurability and disjointness of the pieces are used exactly once, for the countable additivity that reassembles mu_H over S.
main_results.truncation: hausdorffMeasure_truncated_add_le: (n - m) + m >= n holds in N whether or not m <= n, and the Hausdorff measure decreases in the exponent, so mu_H[(n-m)+m] S <= mu_H[n] S. This is why N1 needs NO hypothesis relating dim W2 to dim V - the exact point on which the companion diagnostic N2 fails.

proof_shape: For epsilon_j = (j+1)^-1 take the one-scale majorant G_j; the pointwise infimum H = inf_j G_j is measurable, still dominates the slice function, and satisfies the bound at every scale. Positivity of dim W2 and finiteness of mu_H[n] S make the bound tend to 0, so the integral of H is 0; H is measurable, hence a.e. zero, hence the slice is a.e. null.

why_this_is_not_progress.the_exponent: N1 delivers n - dim W2. In the route's notation W2 is the orthogonal complement of the rank-r range in the m-dimensional target, so dim W2 = m - r and the exponent is k + r, NOT k. Recorded as N1_exponent_is_k_add_r.
why_this_is_not_progress.weaker_in_the_useless_direction: for r >= 1 a mu_H[k+r]-null statement implies nothing about mu_H[k]: at the exponent k = n - r every set of positive Lebesgue measure has INFINITE Hausdorff measure. Recorded as N1_null_at_higher_exponent_says_nothing_at_k, a specialization of the repaired N2 proved in the preceding round.
why_this_is_not_progress.R0_does_not_depend_on_it: R0 was proved independently by slicing INSIDE A FIBRE (Analysis/StratumSlicing.lean), where k + (m - r) = n - r is the right exponent. Analysis/ExponentObstruction.lean has no downstream consumer.

side_conditions_are_real.positive_codimension: 0 < finrank W2 is necessary. N1_needs_positive_codimension refutes N1 WITH THAT HYPOTHESIS DELETED, at the Type instance implied by the route's Type* version: take V = W = R, W2 zero-dimensional, Q = 0, u = id, S = [0,1]; the piece hypothesis holds trivially because Q . u is constant, the single fibre is all of S, and mu_H[1] S = 1, not 0. With dim W2 = 0 the Eilenberg constant epsilon^(dim W2) is 1 and nothing tends to zero.
side_conditions_are_real.measurability_of_S: used exactly once, for the countable additivity that turns the sum of the pieces' Eilenberg right-hand sides back into mu_H of S
